title: Every step completion ships the entire accumulated host transcript to the Flow Canvas (quadratic IPC churn on long runs)
existing_state: When the Flow Canvas window is open, Form1.SshService_StepCompleted (Form1.cs:13620-13650) attaches variables = activeContext?.GetAllVariables() (Form1.cs:13636) to the execution-update message sent for every completed step. ScriptContext.GetAllVariables (Services/Scripting/ScriptContext.cs:606-618) injects _output = LastCommandOutput and _outputwindow = OutputWindowText (lines 615-616), where OutputWindowText (lines 488-496) returns the FULL pane-formatted transcript accumulated for the host so far. FlowCanvasForm.SendMessage (UI/FlowCanvasForm.cs:337-362) runs JsonConvert.SerializeObject on the whole payload per call and posts it cross-process via PostWebMessageAsJson, where React must JSON.parse it again. There is no truncation or size guard anywhere on this path. Net effect: total bytes shipped grow as O(steps x transcript size) — quadratic in run length. A loop issuing 500 sends with ~2KB output each means the final execution-update messages each carry 1MB+, and a single host's run pushes hundreds of MB of serialize/IPC/parse churn; multiply by per-host execution and per-iteration step events. Users see the canvas (and the app, since posting marshals to the shared UI thread) get progressively more sluggish during exactly the runs this preset-builder is for.
recommendation: Strip _outputwindow (and consider capping _output and any individual value to a few KB with a truncation marker) from the variables payload built for execution-update — either filter in SshService_StepCompleted before sending, or add a ScriptContext.GetCanvasVariablesSnapshot() that excludes transcript pseudo-variables. Keep the full snapshot only for debug-paused (Form1.cs:13683), which is rare and genuinely needs inspection data. Optionally stop sending variables on every step entirely and only send when the variables panel is visible or on pause/branch events.
user_benefit: Long multi-host script runs and big loops stop degrading the canvas and UI thread; memory/GC churn during runs drops by orders of magnitude on output-heavy scripts.

evidence.note: execution-update built per StepCompleted with variables = GetAllVariables(), no size guard
GetAllVariables injects _outputwindow = full accumulated host transcript (StringBuilder.ToString of the whole run so far)
SendMessage serializes the full payload per call and posts via PostWebMessageAsJson (cross-process string copy)
